scope: Desktop Chromium, actual Regular TTF; primary DPR1, DPR2 regression; not Flutter/Android acceptance

glyph_observations.U+6525: At DPR1 the middle framed area develops more horizontal separation instead of one uniform dense gray block. It remains crowded at native 14px, and the three counters are not claimed to be independently obvious in every native rendering. DPR2 shows the three framed spaces more clearly. The bamboo top and overall balance do not look conspicuously displaced or distorted.
glyph_observations.U+87A3: The lower internal opening/terminal-dot region is slightly less crowded. The change is smaller than the U+6525 change; DPR1 still has tightly packed central and lower strokes. Dot and lower-stroke weight are retained, with no observed broken structure or clipping. DPR2 shows no obvious structural regression in the reviewed sample.

visual_review.native_size_conclusion: Localized, conservative improvement in the labeled 14 CSS px Regular TTF comparison. The effect is easier to inspect in the pixel zoom than in the native PNG; dense DPR1 text remains difficult. This is not a blind recognition experiment or a guarantee of small-size readability.
visual_review.fairness: Both versions use actual sfnt/glyf TTF resources, same size, width, line height, y position, foreground/background and physical sampling phase. Target/phrase pixels change while both unchanged control texts have zero changed pixels in every theme/DPR.
visual_review.limits: Desktop Chromium TTF only, DPR1 primary with DPR2 regression. It does not prove all counters improve on every rasterizer, alter WOFF2 behavior, or establish Flutter/Android real-chart acceptance.
